verified.exploit_entry_point: The library's public URL-safety API, reached through both surfaces the repository ships: the package's declared entry (package.json main -> dist/utils.js -> dist/helpers.js, the committed build a consumer loads) and the TypeScript source module the package is built from (src/utils.ts, compiled by the verifier with the project's own tsc). Security cases call is_url_safe, is_redirect_safe and is_url_safe_debug on literal URLs; nothing computes an expected value with product code.
sites: src/helpers.ts:504-542 (is_url_safe strips the separator from the whole URL before parsing and resolves the rewritten host)
src/helpers.ts:451-486 (is_redirect_safe strips the separator from the initial URL, and each hop is only checked for scheme and host, not credentials)
src/helpers.ts:545-546 (is_url_safe_debug keeps the old normalisation and never applies a credential check)
dist/helpers.js:383-461 (the committed build of the same three functions, loaded by the package entry)
tsconfig.json:1-12 (the pinned build configuration does not build into the layout package main loads)
routes: T1: credential-bearing authority through the main check (source surface)
T2: the same through the package entry the committed build supplies
T3: credential-bearing initial URL and credential-bearing redirect targets through the redirect walker
T5 (coupled, functional): an at-sign in the path or query, and the exported at-sign helper, keep working
services: a local HTTP service on 127.0.0.1, started by tests/test.sh; its names are reserved in the container's hosts file and the DNS classifier does not resolve them offline
verified.project_tests_run: The project has no test runner (package.json test exits 1) and no test files; the only exercise code is benches/ssrf-validation.bench.ts (vitest bench, no assertions), which is not a pass/fail suite. The hidden functional suite covers the public API and the exported helper the bench exercises. The pinned tree, the reference fix and every check patch were run through both hidden suites: 15 security and 18 functional cases.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one URL and the check does look like it parses and resolves a host, so the normalisation step reads as hardening rather than the defect

wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the library decides whether a URL may be fetched; there is no resource, owner or proxy object to confuse
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions; every caller uses the same predicate
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the checks are pure predicates; there is no read/write or verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority or secret lookup; failing closed on an empty DNS answer is load-bearing for offline legitimate URLs and the property does not require a resolution

A.summary: SSRF validation bypass by parser differential on the URL authority: credentials were removed from the string before the host was judged
